tabs.title: Business issues
tabs.html: Historically it takes two analysts a week to prepare the quarterly board reports. There is also usually at least one issue each quarter where a value is wrong because of a bad cell reference in an Excel formula. On occasion there are conflicting results because the products and departments that roll up to each business unit are not defined consistently.

tabs.title: Requirements
tabs.html:
Planned changes

Contoso plans to automate and standardize the quarterly reporting with Power BI, reduce the time to populate the reports to less than two days and create common logic for business units, products and departments, used across all reports.

Technical requirements

  • Reports and datasets refreshed with minimum manual effort.
  • A single package of reports for the board with custom navigation and links to supplementary information.
  • Maintenance, including manually updating data and access, must be minimized.

Security requirements

The reports must be available to the board from powerbi.com using an Azure AD group. For analysts:

  • Access all balance sheet and product catalog data.
  • Access only the profit and loss data of their business unit.
  • Can create new reports from the profit and loss dataset, but those reports must NOT be included in the quarterly board reports.
  • Must NOT be able to share the quarterly reports with anyone.
  • Must NOT be able to make new reports using the balance sheet data.

Report requirements

You plan to relate the balance sheet table to a date table in a many-to-one relationship based on the last day of the month. At least one balance sheet report must show ending balances for the quarter and for the previous quarter. The date table will contain these columns:

  • Ending balances of each account.
  • Changes in long-term liabilities from the previous quarter.
  • Percent of total revenue contributed by each product category.
  • Comparison of quarterly revenue versus the same quarter of the previous year.

The reports must be updated with the latest data by 5 AM each day.

tabs.title: Report requirements
tabs.html:
Northwind requires the reports Top Products, Top Customers and On-Time Shipping.

  • Top Customers: top 20 customers by highest sales amount in a selected order month or quarter, product category and sales region.
  • Top Products: top 20 products by highest sales amount in a selected order month or quarter, sales region and product category; must also show which suppliers provide the top products.
  • On-Time Shipping: for a selected shipping month or quarter, the percentage of orders shipped late by country and shipping region, and customers with multiple late shipments during the last quarter.

Late orders are those shipped after the required shipping date. The warehouse shipping department must be notified if the percentage of late orders within the current month exceeds 5%. Reports must show historical data for the current calendar year and the last three calendar years.

tabs.title: Technical and security requirements
tabs.html:
Technical requirements

  • A single dataset must support all three reports.
  • The reports must be stored in a single Power BI workspace.
  • Report data must be current as of 7 AM Pacific Time each day.
  • Fast response times when users interact with a visualization.
  • The data model must minimize the dataset size while meeting the requirements.

Security requirements

Access must be granted to Azure AD security groups only (one exists per department). The sales department must be able to:

  • Create, edit and delete content in the reports.
  • Manage permissions for workspaces, datasets and reports.
  • Publish, unpublish, update and change the permissions for an app.
  • Assign Azure AD groups role-based access to the reports workspace.

Sales users must access only the data of the sales region assigned to them in Sales Employees. This RLS table filter DAX expression is applied to Sales Employees:

[EmailAddress] = USERNAME()

RLS applies only to sales users; users in all other departments must be able to view all the data.

q001.stem:
You plan to create the Power BI model shown in the exhibit.

Refresh requirements: Customer, daily; Date, once every three years; Sales, near real time; SalesAggregate, once per week.

You must select the storage mode for each table. The solution must minimize the load times of visuals and load the data into the model according to the refresh requirements.

Which storage mode should you select for each table? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Customer: Dual
  • Date: Dual
  • Sales: DirectQuery
  • SalesAggregate: Import

Why it is correct (table by table):

  • Sales → DirectQuery: it must be near real time; only DirectQuery queries the source on each interaction without waiting for a scheduled refresh.
  • SalesAggregate → Import: it is an aggregation table refreshed weekly; cached in Import it answers summarized queries fastest (the classic aggregations pattern: aggregate in Import + detail in DirectQuery).
  • Customer → Dual: it is a dimension related to Sales (DirectQuery) and to the aggregate (Import). In Dual it can answer from cache or query the source, avoiding limited relationships and improving performance.
  • Date → Dual: same reasoning as Customer; it also changes very rarely, so its cache is stable.

Why not the others: Customer/Date in Import would create limited relationships (many-to-one across different sources) with the DirectQuery table, hurting performance; Customer/Date in DirectQuery cannot be served from cache; Sales in Import would break the near-real-time requirement, and SalesAggregate in DirectQuery would lose the cached-aggregation benefit.

  • Official documentation: Storage mode in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn | Use aggregations in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn

q002.stem:
You have a project management app that is fully hosted in Microsoft Teams. The app was developed by using Microsoft Power Apps.

You need to create a Power BI report that connects to the project management app. Which connector should you select?
options: Microsoft Teams Personal Analytics
SQL Server database
Dataverse
Dataflows

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Dataverse

Why it is correct: Power Apps apps hosted in Teams store their data in Dataverse for Teams (a Dataverse environment built into the team). The Dataverse connector is therefore the one that reaches those tables from Power BI.

  • Official documentation: Dataverse connector - Microsoft Learn | Dataverse for Teams overview - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Microsoft Teams Personal Analytics — Why it is incorrect: it is a connector for personal Teams usage analytics; it does not expose the data of a Power Apps app.
  • Option B — SQL Server database — Why it is incorrect: the app data is not in a directly reachable SQL Server database; it lives in Dataverse for Teams.
  • Option D — Dataflows — Why it is incorrect: a dataflow is a data-preparation layer you would have to build first; it is not where the app stores its data.

q003.stem:
For the sales department, you publish a Power BI report that imports data from an Excel file located in a SharePoint folder. The data model contains several measures.

You need to create a Power BI report from the existing data. The solution must minimize development effort. Which type of data source should you use?
options: A Power BI dataset (semantic model)
A SharePoint folder
Power BI dataflows
An Excel workbook

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: A Power BI dataset (semantic model)

Why it is correct: the already published semantic model contains the relationships and measures. Connecting to it (live connection) lets you build a new report reusing all that work, without repeating loading or modeling.

  • Official documentation: Reuse semantic models across workspaces - Microsoft Learn | Separate reports from models - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — A SharePoint folder — Why it is incorrect: you would start from scratch with the source: reload the data, remodel it and rewrite the measures.
  • Option C — Power BI dataflows — Why it is incorrect: dataflows prepare reusable data but do not contain the existing model measures; you would need to build another model on top.
  • Option D — An Excel workbook — Why it is incorrect: same as the SharePoint folder: you would rebuild the model and measures from the file.

q004.stem:
You import two Excel tables named Customer and Address into Power Query.

Customer: Customer ID, Customer Name, Phone, Email Address, Address ID. Address: Address ID, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City, State/Region, Country, Postal Code.

Each Customer ID is a unique customer and each Address ID a unique address. You need a query with one row per customer containing City, State/Region and Country. What should you do?
options: Merge the Customer and Address tables.
Group the Customer and Address tables by the Address ID column.
Transpose the Customer and Address tables.
Append the Customer and Address tables.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Merge the Customer and Address tables.

Why it is correct: merge is a JOIN-type operation: it adds Address columns to each Customer row matching on Address ID, and since both keys are unique the result keeps one row per customer.

  • Official documentation: Merge queries overview - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Group the Customer and Address tables by the Address ID column. — Why it is incorrect: grouping aggregates rows of one table; it does not bring columns from another query. Official documentation: Group by - Microsoft Learn
  • Option C — Transpose the Customer and Address tables. — Why it is incorrect: transposing rotates rows and columns; it does not relate the two tables. Official documentation: Transpose a table - Microsoft Learn
  • Option D — Append the Customer and Address tables. — Why it is incorrect: append stacks rows of tables with the same structure (UNION); here the columns differ and you would not get one row per customer. Official documentation: Append queries - Microsoft Learn

q005.stem:
You have two Azure SQL databases that contain the same tables and columns. For each database, you create a query that retrieves data from a table named Customer.

You need to combine the Customer tables into a single table. The solution must minimize the size of the data model and support scheduled refresh in powerbi.com.

What should you do? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option to use to combine the Customer tables: Append Queries as New
  • Action on the two original queries: Disable loading the query to the data model

Analysis:

  • Append Queries as New: both tables have the same columns and you want to stack rows, so you append. “as New” creates a new query and leaves both originals untouched as its sources. (Merge adds columns, not rows.)
  • Disable loading the query to the data model: the original queries are intermediate steps; if loaded they would duplicate the data in the model. Disabling load keeps them in Power Query (they still refresh and feed the final query) without using memory. Deleting them would break the appended query, and “Disable including in report refresh” would stop them from refreshing.
  • Official documentation: Append queries - Microsoft Learn | Query overview in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn

links.t: Query overview in Power BI Desktop

q006.stem:
In Power Query Editor, you have three queries named ProductCategory, ProductSubCategory and Product.

Every Product has a ProductSubCategory. Not every ProductSubCategory has a parent ProductCategory.

You need to merge the three queries into a single query with the best performance in Power Query. Which join kind do you use for each merge? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Product ↔ ProductSubCategory: Inner
  • ProductSubCategory ↔ ProductCategory: Left outer
  • Product → ProductSubCategory: Inner. Every Product row has its subcategory, so no rows are lost; the inner join is the most efficient.
  • ProductSubCategory → ProductCategory: Left outer. Some subcategories have no parent category; left outer keeps all left rows (subcategories) and brings categories where they exist. An inner join would drop those subcategories and therefore products.
  • Official documentation: Inner join - Microsoft Learn | Left outer join - Microsoft Learn

q007.stem:
You are building a Power BI report that uses data from an Azure SQL database named erp. You import the tables: Products (catalog), Orders (high-level order information) and Order Line Items (product ID, quantity and price per line).

You need to analyze orders sold over time with a measure of the total order value, and orders by attributes of the products sold. The solution must minimize update times when interacting with visuals. What should you do first?
options: From Power Query, merge the Order Line Items query and the Products query.
Create a calculated column that adds a list of product categories to the Orders table by using a DAX function.
Calculate the count of orders per product by using a DAX function.
From Power Query, merge the Orders query and the Order Line Items query.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: From Power Query, merge the Orders query and the Order Line Items query.

Why it is correct: this is the header/detail pattern: the best practice is to flatten the header (Orders) into the detail (Order Line Items) so you have a single fact table at line level related to Products. That avoids chained fact tables and makes visual queries faster.

  • Official documentation: Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI - Microsoft Learn | Fact tables - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — From Power Query, merge the Order Line Items query and the Products query. — Why it is incorrect: merging lines with products would denormalize the catalog into the fact table, increasing its size and leaving Orders as a second chained fact table.
  • Option B — Create a calculated column that adds a list of product categories to the Orders table by using a DAX function. — Why it is incorrect: calculated columns holding category lists are costly, consume memory and do not solve the header/detail design.
  • Option C — Calculate the count of orders per product by using a DAX function. — Why it is incorrect: a count per product does not prepare the model to analyze order value or product attributes; it is a calculation, not a model change.

links.t: Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI

q008.stem:
You have a SharePoint Online site that contains several document libraries. One of them contains manufacturing reports saved as Excel files, all with the same data structure.

You need to use Power BI Desktop to load only the manufacturing reports to a table for analysis. What should you do?
options: Get data from a SharePoint folder and enter the site URL. Select Transform, then filter by the folder path to the manufacturing reports library.
Get data from a SharePoint list and enter the site URL. Select Combine & Transform, then filter by the folder path to the manufacturing reports library.
Get data from a SharePoint folder, enter the site URL, and then select Combine & Load.
Get data from a SharePoint list, enter the site URL, and then select Combine & Load.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Get data from a SharePoint folder and enter the site URL. Select Transform, then filter by the folder path to the manufacturing reports library.

Why it is correct: the SharePoint folder connector returns all files on the site (from every library). Transform opens Power Query so you can filter on the manufacturing library path before combining, loading only those files.

  • Official documentation: SharePoint folder - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Get data from a SharePoint list and enter the site URL. Select Combine & Transform, then filter by the folder path to the manufacturing reports library. — Why it is incorrect: a SharePoint list is tabular content (tasks, calendars), not the Excel files in a library.
  • Option C — Get data from a SharePoint folder, enter the site URL, and then select Combine & Load. — Why it is incorrect: Combine & Load would combine files from every library on the site without filtering to the manufacturing library.
  • Option D — Get data from a SharePoint list, enter the site URL, and then select Combine & Load. — Why it is incorrect: it uses the list connector, which does not read Excel files, and it does not filter either.

q009.stem:
You have an Excel workbook with two sheets, Sheet1 and Sheet2, containing tables Table1 and Table2. You need to use Power Query Editor to combine the products from Table1 and Table2 into a table with one column and no duplicate values.

Which three actions should you perform, and in what order?

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Step 1: From Power BI Desktop, import the data from Excel, and select Table1 and Table2
  • Step 2: From Power Query Editor, append Table2 to Table1
  • Step 3: From Power Query Editor, select Table1, and then select Remove duplicates
  1. Import Table1 and Table2 from Excel (without data in Power Query there is nothing to combine).
  2. Append Table2 to Table1: you want to stack rows (products from both), not add columns.
  3. Remove duplicates on the resulting table.

“Merge” adds columns, and “remove errors” is unnecessary because the data has no errors.

Note: step 3 says “select Table1”; after appending, Table1 is the query holding the combined result, which is why duplicates are removed from it.

⚠️ Heads-up: the source solution image shows: append → remove errors → remove duplicates (no import first). The community (top-voted answer) proposes import → append → remove duplicates, which is what is marked here; “remove errors” makes no sense because the data has no errors. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Append queries - Microsoft Learn | Remove duplicates - Microsoft Learn

q010.stem:
You have a CSV file that contains user complaints. The Logged column contains the date and time of each complaint in the format 2018-12-31 at 08:59.

You need to analyze the complaints by logged date and use a built-in date hierarchy. What should you do?
options: Apply a transformation to extract the last 11 characters of the Logged column and set the data type of the new column to Date.
Change the data type of the Logged column to Date.
Split the Logged column by using at as the delimiter.
Apply a transformation to extract the first 11 characters of the Logged column.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Split the Logged column by using at as the delimiter.

Why it is correct: splitting on the delimiter “ at ” separates the date (2018-12-31) from the time (08:59) into two columns. The date column is typed as Date and enables the built-in date hierarchy (year, quarter, month, day).

  • Official documentation: Split columns by delimiter - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Apply a transformation to extract the last 11 characters of the Logged column and set the data type of the new column to Date. — Why it is incorrect: the last 11 characters are roughly “ at 08:59” (the time), not the date; the text would not convert to Date either.
  • Option B — Change the data type of the Logged column to Date. — Why it is incorrect: the full text “2018-12-31 at 08:59” is not a recognizable date format and the type change would produce errors. Official documentation: Data types in Power Query - Microsoft Learn
  • Option D — Apply a transformation to extract the first 11 characters of the Logged column. — Why it is incorrect: extracting the first 11 characters leaves “2018-12-31 ” as untyped text and needs another step; splitting on a delimiter is the idiomatic, robust approach (it does not depend on character count).

You have an Excel file in a OneDrive folder. The file must be imported to a Power BI dataset (semantic model).

You need to ensure that the dataset can be refreshed in powerbi.com. Which two connectors can you use? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

Web

  • Option E: Web

Why it is correct: a OneDrive file is reachable by cloud URL, so the service can refresh without a gateway using the SharePoint folder connector (OneDrive for Business sits on SharePoint) or the Web connector with the file link.

  • Option B — Text/CSV — Why it is incorrect: with local file paths the same applies: it needs a gateway to refresh in the service.

q012.stem:
You are profiling data in Power Query Editor. The Reports table has a State column whose distribution and quality metrics are shown in the exhibit: 96% valid, 0% error, 4% empty; 69 distinct, 4 unique.

Select the answer choice that completes each statement based on the exhibit. NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Number of different values in State including nulls: 69
  • Non-null values that occur only once: 4
  • 69: “distinct” is the total number of different values found in the column (each distinct value counted once, null included).
  • 4: “unique” is the number of values that appear exactly once.

Distinct ≠ unique: distinct counts different values even if repeated; unique counts only those that never repeat.

  • Official documentation: Data profiling tools - Microsoft Learn

q013.stem:
You have two CSV files: Products (ProductID, ProductName, SupplierID, CategoryID) and Categories (CategoryID, CategoryName, CategoryDescription). You import them into Power Query Editor from Power BI Desktop.

You need a model with a single table named Product containing ProductID, ProductName, SupplierID, CategoryID, CategoryName and CategoryDescription. How should you combine the queries and what should you do on the Categories query? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Combine the queries by performing a: Merge
  • On the Categories query: Disable the query load.
  • Merge: you add columns (CategoryName, CategoryDescription) to Products matching on CategoryID; append would stack rows.
  • Disable the query load: Categories is only an intermediate step; not loading it avoids an unnecessary table in the model (it stays available for the merge). Deleting it would break the merge and excluding it from refresh would leave stale data.
  • Official documentation: Merge queries overview - Microsoft Learn | Query overview in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn
