q085.stem:
You are building a financial report using Power BI. You have a table financials with a Date column and a Sales column. You need to create a measure that calculates the relative change in sales compared to the previous quarter. How do you complete the measure? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

Sales QoQ% =
IF(
  ISFILTERED('financials'[Date]),
  ERROR("Uh oh."),
  VAR PREV_QUARTER =
    [A] ( SUM('financials'[Sales]),
      [B] ( 'financials'[Date].[Date], -1, QUARTER ) )
  RETURN
    [C] ( SUM('financials'[Sales]) - PREV_QUARTER, PREV_QUARTER )
)

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • [A]: CALCULATE
  • [B]: DATEADD
  • [C]: DIVIDE
  • CALCULATE: evaluates the sum of sales in another time context.
  • DATEADD (−1, QUARTER): shifts dates back one quarter.
  • DIVIDE: (sales − previous quarter) / previous quarter = relative change, with safe divide-by-zero handling.
  • Official documentation: DATEADD (DAX) - Microsoft Learn | DIVIDE (DAX) - Microsoft Learn

q088.stem:
You are creating a Power BI model with a Store table (StoreName, City, State/Province, Country, all text). You plan to create a map visual showing store locations with drill-down from Country to State/Province to City.

What should you do to ensure the locations are mapped properly?
options: Change the data type of City, State/Province and Country.
Set Summarization for City, State/Province and Country to Don’t summarize.
Set the data category of City, State/Province and Country.

  • Official documentation: Data categorization in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn

q089.stem: You are building a data model for a Power BI report. You have a table with a Machine-User column with values like “ABC-657” and a download-size column in MB. You need to create a clustered bar chart that shows Machine and User separately. What should you do?

You need to create a date table in Power BI that must contain 10 full calendar years, including the current year. How should you complete the DAX expression?

Date =
VAR var1 = [A] ( [B]() )
RETURN
  [C] ( DATE( var1 - 9, 01, 01 ), DATE( var1, 12, 31 ) )

answer.correct:

  • [A]: YEAR
  • [B]: TODAY
  • [C]: CALENDAR
  • YEAR(TODAY()): gets the current year.
  • CALENDAR(start, end): returns a table with a column of contiguous dates between the two given dates, inclusive (Jan 1 nine years ago to Dec 31 of this year = 10 full years). CALENDARAUTO takes no start/end dates.

q091.stem:

answer.correct:

  • [B]: 'Date'[Date]
  • TOTALYTD: evaluates the expression from the first day of the year through the last date of the dates column in the current context.

q093.stem:
You are modifying a Power BI model with a Sales table (Transaction ID, Customer Key, Sales Date Key, Sales Amount) and a Transaction Size table: Small (0–10,000), Medium (10,001–100,000), Large (100,001–999,999,999).

You need a calculated column that classifies each transaction as small, medium or large by Sales Amount. How should you complete the expression?

Transaction Size =
VAR SalesTotal = 'Sales'[SalesAmount]
VAR FilteringSegment = [A] ( 'Transaction Size',
  [B] ( 'Transaction Size'[Min] <= SalesTotal, 'Transaction Size'[Max] >= SalesTotal ) )
VAR Result = [C] ( DISTINCT( 'Transaction Size'[Transaction Size] ), FilteringSegment )
RETURN Result

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • [A]: CALCULATE
  • [B]: AND
  • [C]: FILTER
  • CALCULATE: evaluates the table under a modified filter.
  • AND: requires the amount to be between min and max (both conditions at once).
  • FILTER: returns the distinct Transaction Size values that satisfy the segment condition.

One-to-many relationship from Suppliers to LineItems on ID/Supplier ID.

Remove the LineItems[Description] column.
Remove the rows from LineItems where LineItems[Invoice Date] is before the beginning of last month.
Group LineItems by LineItems[Invoice ID] and LineItems[Invoice Date] with a sum of LineItems[Price].

  • Option D: Remove Posts[Full Text] and Posts[Summary].

Why it is correct: filtering Traffic to blog visits discards rows no visual uses, and removing Posts’ long text columns Full Text and Summary (unused) reduces the load volume.

q097.stem:
You have the Power BI model shown (dimDate and Sales). The Sales table contains records of sales by day for the last five years until today’s date.

You plan to create a measure that returns the total sales of March 2021 when March 2022 is selected. Which DAX expression should you use?
options: CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Sales]), PREVIOUSYEAR(dimDate[Date]))
TOTALYTD(SUM(Sales[Sales]), dimDate[Date])
CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Sales]), SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(dimDate[Date]))
SUM(Sales[Sales])

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Sales]), SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(dimDate[Date]))

Why it is correct: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR shifts the dates in the current context back exactly one year (March 2022 → March 2021) and CALCULATE evaluates the sum over that period.

  • Official documentation: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR (DAX) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Sales]), PREVIOUSYEAR(dimDate[Date])) — Why it is incorrect: PREVIOUSYEAR returns the whole previous year (all of 2021), not just March. Official documentation: PREVIOUSYEAR (DAX) - Microsoft Learn
  • Option B — TOTALYTD(SUM(Sales[Sales]), dimDate[Date]) — Why it is incorrect: TOTALYTD accumulates from the start of the year to date, not the same month of the previous year. Official documentation: TOTALYTD (DAX) - Microsoft Learn
  • Option D — SUM(Sales[Sales]) — Why it is incorrect: a plain sum depends only on the current filter (March 2022).

q100.stem:

q101.stem:
You have a Power BI data model with tables Products and Sales and a one-to-many relationship. You have a report with a report-level filter for Products.

You need a measure that returns the percent of total sales for each product. The measure must respect the report-level filter when calculating the total. How do you complete the DAX measure?

Percent of Product Sales =
VAR ProductSales = SUM('Sales'[Sales])
VAR AllSales =
  [A] ( SUM('Sales'[Sales]), [B] ( 'Products'[Product] ) )
RETURN DIVIDE(ProductSales, AllSales)

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • [A]: CALCULATE
  • [B]: ALLSELECTED
  • CALCULATE: modifies the filter context for the denominator.
  • ALLSELECTED: removes the visual’s own filters (the product row) but keeps external ones such as the report-level filter, so the total respects it. ALL would ignore it.

⚠️ Heads-up: in the source image the second box shows FILTER, which is not syntactically valid with a column; the community (majority) and the documentation point to ALLSELECTED, which is what is marked. Check it against the linked documentation.

q102.stem:
You have a Power BI data model that analyzes product sales over time, with tables Product (Product ID, Product Name, Product Category) and Sales (Product ID, Order Date, Ship Date, Delivered Date, Invoice Number, Quantity, Sales Amount). A one-to-many relationship exists between the tables and the auto date/time option is enabled.

You need to reduce the size of the model while maintaining the ability to analyze product sales by month and quarter. Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: Create a relationship between the Date table and the Sales table.
Disable the auto date/time option.
Create a Date table and select Mark as Date Table.
Disable the load on the Date table.
Remove the relationship between the Product table and the Sales table.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option A: Create a relationship between the Date table and the Sales table.
  • Option C: Create a Date table and select Mark as Date Table.

Why it is correct: with auto date/time, Power BI creates a hidden date table for each date column (here three: order, ship, delivery), increasing size. A single Date table marked as date table and related to Sales provides month and quarter and avoids those hidden tables.

⚠️ Heads-up: the community also proposes B + C (disable auto date/time and create a Date table); the source key is AC (10 votes vs 5). Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Apply auto date/time in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn | Set and use date tables - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Disable the auto date/time option. — Why it is incorrect: disabling the option alone is not enough: without its own date table month/quarter analysis is lost.
  • Option D — Disable the load on the Date table. — Why it is incorrect: disabling load on the Date table removes it from the model, losing month/quarter analysis.
  • Option E — Remove the relationship between the Product table and the Sales table. — Why it is incorrect: removing the Product–Sales relationship prevents sales-by-product analysis.

q105.stem: You have a CSV file with user complaints; the Logged column contains date and time in the format 2018-12-31 at 08:59. You need to analyze complaints by logged date and use a built-in date hierarchy. What should you do?
options: Apply a transformation to extract the first 11 characters of the Logged column.
Add a conditional column that outputs 2018 if the Logged column starts with 2018 and set the data type of the new column to Whole Number.
Create a column by example that starts with 2018-12-31 and set the data type of the new column to Date.
Apply a transformation to extract the last 11 characters of the Logged column and set the data type of the new column to Date.

Correct answer:

  • Option C: Create a column by example that starts with 2018-12-31 and set the data type of the new column to Date.

q108.stem:
You use Power Query Editor to preview a query with sales order data: Tax Amount, Sales Order ID, Freight Amount, Subtotal Amount and Total Item Quantity. Subtotal Amount and Total Item Quantity are always populated, but Tax Amount and Freight Amount are sometimes null when an order has no associated amount.

In the Tax Amount column, remove rows that contain null values.
In the Freight Amount column, remove rows that contain null values.

q109.stem:

q111.stem:
You have the model shown (Product, Sales, Date). The Sales table has: ProductID (whole), InvoiceNumber (whole), OrderDate (date), ShipDate (date), SalesAmount (decimal), SalesQuantity (whole), LastUpdated (date/time, e.g. 5/22/2022 11:45:30 AM), AuditID (whole). [Employee Name] - USERPRINCIPALNAME()

q114.stem:
You have the model shown: Country (Country, Email, Manager) with 1:* relationships to Sales and to Human Resources. Country contains: USA/CFO/cfo@msn.com, France/Phillipe/phillipe@msn.com, Brazil/Juan/juan@msn.com, Singapore/Srini/srini@msn.com. You create two RLS roles, Manager and CFO, and will publish the dataset to the Power BI service.

You need to create the DAX filter expressions: each manager sees only the Sales and Human Resources data of their own country; the CFO must be prevented from seeing Human Resources; the CFO must see the sales of all countries. Drag the expressions to the targets (each may be used once, more than once or not at all).

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Human Resources:: [Manager]="CFO"
  • Country:: [Email]=userprincipalname()
  • Country → [Email]=userprincipalname(): each user sees their country row and the filter propagates to Sales and Human Resources through the relationships.
  • Human Resources → [Manager]="CFO": this is the source key for the Human Resources table.

⚠️ Heads-up: the logic of this exercise is debatable: to stop the CFO seeing Human Resources False() on that table would be natural (and Human Resources has no Manager column). The source key is marked; please review. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Row-level security (RLS) with Power BI - Microsoft Learn

q115.stem: You have a Power BI data model that imports data from an Excel spreadsheet. You use Power Query to load a query that contains renamed and custom columns. Later, you attempt to reload the query and receive: “Expression.Error: The column ‘Category’ of the table wasn’t found.” What are two possible causes of the error? Each correct answer presents a complete explanation.
options: The column was removed from the source file.
The column was renamed in the source file.
The file is no longer in the specified location.
The data type of the column was changed.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option A: The column was removed from the source file.
  • Option B: The column was renamed in the source file.

Why it is correct: Power Query steps reference the column by name; if it is removed or renamed in the source, the step fails with “column wasn’t found”.

  • Official documentation: Power Query user interface - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option C — The file is no longer in the specified location. — Why it is incorrect: if the file is missing the error is a data-source error (file not found), not a column error.
  • Option D — The data type of the column was changed. — Why it is incorrect: a data type change does not cause “column not found”; at most a conversion error.

q116.stem: You have a model with a Sales table (Order Line ID, Product ID, Unit Price, Order ID, Quantity). Orders are uniquely identified by Order ID and can have multiple order lines; each order line within an order has a different Product ID. You need a DAX measure that counts the number of orders. Which formula should you use?
options: Count('Sales'[Order ID])
CountA('Sales'[Order ID])
CountRows('Sales')
DistinctCount('Sales'[Order ID])

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: DistinctCount('Sales'[Order ID])

Why it is correct: an order appears in several rows (one per line); DISTINCTCOUNT counts each Order ID once.

⚠️ Heads-up: 32% of the community voted A; the official key and majority (67%) is D, the only option counting distinct orders. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: DISTINCTCOUNT (DAX) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Count('Sales'[Order ID]) — Why it is incorrect: COUNT counts all non-blank rows, i.e. lines, not orders. Official documentation: COUNT (DAX) - Microsoft Learn
  • Option B — CountA('Sales'[Order ID]) — Why it is incorrect: COUNTA also counts lines.
  • Option C — CountRows('Sales') — Why it is incorrect: COUNTROWS returns the number of lines.

q117.stem:
You are creating a Power BI model in Power BI Desktop and need a calculated table named Numbers containing all integers from -100 to 100. How should you complete the DAX calculation? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

Numbers = [A] [B]

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • [A]: GENERATESERIES
  • [B]: ( -100, 100, 1 )
  • GENERATESERIES: returns a one-column table with a numeric series.
  • ( -100, 100, 1 ): start value, end value, step.
  • Official documentation: GENERATESERIES (DAX) - Microsoft Learn

q118.stem: In Power Query Editor you have a query Sales Data with columns: Sale date (Date), Product ID (Whole number), Product name (Text), Product category (Text), Customer ID (Whole number). You need to create two queries, Product Dimension and Sales Fact, based on Sales Data. The solution must minimize maintenance effort and dataset size. Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: Reference the Sales Data query to create the new queries.
Disable the load for the Sales Fact query.
Duplicate the Sales Data query to create the new queries.
Clear Include in report refresh for the Sales Data query.
Disable the load for the Sales Data query.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option A: Reference the Sales Data query to create the new queries.
  • Option E: Disable the load for the Sales Data query.

Why it is correct: referencing avoids duplicating source logic (less maintenance), and disabling load on Sales Data avoids loading a redundant staging table into the model (smaller size).

  • Official documentation: Referencing queries - Microsoft Learn | Query overview in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Disable the load for the Sales Fact query. — Why it is incorrect: Sales Fact is a table the model needs.
  • Option C — Duplicate the Sales Data query to create the new queries. — Why it is incorrect: duplicating copies the steps and increases maintenance.
  • Option D — Clear Include in report refresh for the Sales Data query. — Why it is incorrect: excluding it from refresh does not stop it being loaded into the model.

links.t: Query overview in Power BI Desktop

q119.stem: You have a model with a Date table with columns Date, Fiscal Year, Fiscal Quarter, Month Name, Calendar Year, Week Number, Month Number and Calendar Quarter. You need a calculated table based on Date containing only unique combinations of Calendar Year, Calendar Quarter and Calendar Month. Which DAX function should you include?
options: ADDCOLUMNS
CALCULATE
SUMMARIZE
DATATABLE

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: SUMMARIZE

Why it is correct: SUMMARIZE groups by the given columns and returns only unique combinations.

  • Official documentation: SUMMARIZE (DAX) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — ADDCOLUMNS — Why it is incorrect: ADDCOLUMNS adds columns to a table; it does not group or remove duplicates.
  • Option B — CALCULATE — Why it is incorrect: CALCULATE returns a scalar, not a table.
  • Option D — DATATABLE — Why it is incorrect: DATATABLE creates a table from literal data.

q120.stem:
You have a model with tables Date (Date: Date; Month: Text; Year: Integer) and Sales (Sale: Decimal; Date: Date). Date relates to Sales through the Date columns. You need a calculated table with one row per year and a column with total sales per year. How should you complete the DAX calculation? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

SalesSummary = [A] ( Sales, [B], "Sales", SUM(Sales[Sale]) )

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • [A]: SUMMARIZE
  • [B]: Date[Year]
  • SUMMARIZE: groups and aggregates.
  • Date[Year]: grouping by year gives one row per year; Sales is filtered through the relationship with Date.
  • Official documentation: SUMMARIZE (DAX) - Microsoft Learn

q121.stem: You use Power Query Editor to import and preview sales data for 2020 and 2021 from an Excel file: columns Month, 2020 and 2021 with 12 months. You need to shape the query to show three columns: Month, Sales and Year. What should you select in Power Query Editor?
options: Merge columns
Transpose
Unpivot columns
Pivot column

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Unpivot columns

Why it is correct: columns 2020 and 2021 are values of the Year attribute; unpivoting them yields Attribute (Year) and Value (Sales) columns.

  • Official documentation: Unpivot columns - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Merge columns — Why it is incorrect: merge columns concatenates text.
  • Option B — Transpose — Why it is incorrect: transpose rotates the whole table and does not create the requested columns.
  • Option D — Pivot column — Why it is incorrect: pivot does the opposite: turns rows into columns.

q122.stem:
You are creating a Power BI model to analyze inventory with three tables: Date, Product and Inventory. Inventory relates to Date and Product through one-to-many relationships. Inventory is recorded daily with no exceptions; the correct quantity of a product in a month is the last value recorded that month. You need a DAX measure that shows the correct value when analyzing by year, month or date. How should you complete the measure? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

Last Inventory Count = [A] ( SUM ( 'Inventory'[QuantityAvailable] ), [B] ( 'Date'[Date] ) )

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • [A]: Calculate
  • [B]: LastDate
  • Calculate: evaluates the sum in a modified context.
  • LastDate: returns the last date in the context (last day of the month/year), so the last recorded value is used; data is daily with no exceptions, so LASTNONBLANK is not needed.
  • Official documentation: LASTDATE (DAX) - Microsoft Learn | CALCULATE (DAX) - Microsoft Learn

q123.stem:
Note: question from a series with the same scenario; each has a unique solution.

You have a Power BI report that imports a date table and a sales table from an Azure SQL database. The sales table has these date foreign keys: Due Date, Order Date and Delivery Date.

You need to support the analysis of sales over time based on all the date foreign keys.

Solution: From the Fields pane, you rename the date table as Due Date. You use a DAX expression to create Order Date and Delivery Date as calculated tables. You create active relationships between the sales table and each date table.

Does this meet the goal?
options: Yes
No

answer.correct:

Why it is correct: three date tables with active relationships allow analyzing sales by all three dates at the same time (at the cost of duplicating the date table).

  • Official documentation: USERELATIONSHIP (DAX) - Microsoft Learn | Active vs inactive relationships - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — No — Why it is incorrect: it does meet the goal.

q124.stem:
You are creating a Power BI report showing the number of current employees over time (Import mode). Employment data is imported from Azure SQL Database as a monthly snapshot into a Headcount table: one row per employee per month employed, with a date key for the first day of each snapshot month. A related date table covers 2020–2030. You need a semi-additive DAX measure that returns the employee count for the last available date in a year, quarter or month. How should you complete it? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

Headcount = CALCULATE ( [A], [B] )

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • [A]: CountRows('Headcount')
  • [B]: LastDate('Date'[Date])
  • CountRows('Headcount'): there is one row per employee per month, so counting the snapshot rows gives the employees.
  • LastDate('Date'[Date]): takes the last date of the period from the date table, and the relationship filters Headcount to that snapshot.

⚠️ Heads-up: the source key is CountRows + LastDate(Date[Date]), but since snapshots fall on the first day of the month, the month’s LastDate (last day) would not match the date key; please review the reasoning. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: COUNTROWS (DAX) - Microsoft Learn | LASTDATE (DAX) - Microsoft Learn

q125.stem: You have a query All Sales that imports sales data into a Power BI model. You plan to create a star schema by separating columns into separate queries. The solution must use All Sales as the source for three queries (Sales Fact, Product Dimension and Customer Dimension) and minimize maintenance effort. What should you do to create Sales Fact, and for which query should you clear Enable load?

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • To create Sales Fact: Reference the All Sales query
  • Clear Enable load for: All Sales
  • Reference the All Sales query: referenced queries start from the result of All Sales without duplicating its steps.

q126.stem: You have a model with tables Date (Date, Month, Year) and Sales (Sale: amount; Date). Date relates to Sales through the Date columns. The model contains the measure Total Sales = SUM(Sales[Sale]). You need another measure, Previous Quarter, that shows sales one quarter before the selected period. Which DAX calculation should you use?
options: CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], DATEADD ( Date[Date], -1, QUARTER ) )
CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], DATESQTD ( Date[Date] ) )
TOTALQTD ( [Total Sales], Date[Date] )
CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], PARALLELPERIOD ( Date[Date], 1, QUARTER ) )

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], DATEADD ( Date[Date], -1, QUARTER ) )

Why it is correct: DATEADD with -1 QUARTER shifts the selected period back one quarter.

  • Official documentation: DATEADD (DAX) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], DATESQTD ( Date[Date] ) ) — Why it is incorrect: DATESQTD accumulates the quarter to date, not the previous one.
  • Option C — TOTALQTD ( [Total Sales], Date[Date] ) — Why it is incorrect: TOTALQTD is the current quarter-to-date total.
  • Option D — CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], PARALLELPERIOD ( Date[Date], 1, QUARTER ) ) — Why it is incorrect: with interval +1 PARALLELPERIOD moves one quarter forward (future); -1 would be needed. Official documentation: PARALLELPERIOD (DAX) - Microsoft Learn

q127.stem: You have a Power BI model with tables Sales and Date. Sales contains three measures: Order Quantity, Product Cost and Sales Amount. You need to create the visual shown (a matrix with years 2020–2023 as columns and the three measures as rows, with totals). In which section of the Fields well should you place the measures?
options: Columns
Rows
Values
Drill through

Correct answer:

  • Option C: Values

Why it is correct: measures always go in the matrix Values well; to show them as rows you turn on “Values on rows” in the visual settings.

  • Official documentation: Create a matrix visual - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Columns — Why it is incorrect: Columns is for category fields (here Year), not measures.
  • Option B — Rows — Why it is incorrect: Rows is for category fields; measures go in Values.
  • Option D — Drill through — Why it is incorrect: Drill through defines detail pages, not the visual’s content.

q128.stem: You are reviewing a Power BI data model. You have a calculated table defined as ProductList = INTERSECT ( ProductsGroupA, ProductsGroupB ). You need to identify the results of the DAX expression. Which rows will be returned in ProductList?
options: all the rows in ProductsGroupB that have a matching row in ProductsGroupA
all the rows in both tables
all the rows in ProductsGroupA that have a matching row in ProductsGroupB
all the rows in ProductsGroupA that have no matching row in ProductsGroupB

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: all the rows in ProductsGroupA that have a matching row in ProductsGroupB

Why it is correct: INTERSECT returns the rows of the first table that also exist in the second; ordering and duplicates follow the first table.

  • Official documentation: INTERSECT (DAX) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — all the rows in ProductsGroupB that have a matching row in ProductsGroupA — Why it is incorrect: INTERSECT keeps the rows of the first table (A), not B.
  • Option B — all the rows in both tables — Why it is incorrect: that would be a union (UNION). Official documentation: UNION (DAX) - Microsoft Learn
  • Option D — all the rows in ProductsGroupA that have no matching row in ProductsGroupB — Why it is incorrect: that is EXCEPT. Official documentation: EXCEPT (DAX) - Microsoft Learn

q129.stem: You have a Power BI tenant with a workspace containing a dataset datasetA. You need to build a pivot table report in Microsoft Excel using datasetA as the source. The solution must ensure the report can be refreshed to get the latest data from the Power BI service and that all visible data in datasetA is available in Excel. What should you do to connect Excel to datasetA, and which element of datasetA will be incompatible with the Excel connection?

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • To connect Excel to datasetA: Select Analyze in Excel
  • Incompatible with the Excel connection: Field parameters
  • Analyze in Excel: creates a live connection to the dataset, refreshable and with the whole model available to PivotTables.
  • Field parameters: are not supported in Analyze in Excel.

q132.stem: You have a Power BI semantic model with item, price and country data, displayed in a report that uses filters. You need to calculate the average item price for a given country and the solution must support the existing filters. Which type of quick measure should you use?
options: Total for category (filters applied)
Average per category
Rolling average
Weighted average per category

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Average per category

Why it is correct: “Average per category” computes the average of a value per category (here country) and respects the report filters.

  • Official documentation: Use quick measures - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Total for category (filters applied) — Why it is incorrect: returns a total, not an average.
  • Option C — Rolling average — Why it is incorrect: a rolling average needs a date axis and is not per country.
  • Option D — Weighted average per category — Why it is incorrect: a weighted average needs a weight field that is not mentioned.

q133.stem: You use Power Query Editor to import three tables: Customers, Address and Country. In the source system, not every customer has a related address, but every address has a related country. You need to merge all the tables into a single query and the solution must optimize query refresh performance. Which join type should you use for each merge operation?

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Join Customers with Address: Right outer
  • Join Address with Country: Inner
  • Address with Country → Inner: every address has a country, so the inner join loses no rows and is the most efficient.
  • Customers with Address → Right outer: this is the source key.

⚠️ Heads-up: if you want to keep all customers even without an address, Left outer (Customers on the left) would be the logical choice; the source key is Right outer. Please review. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Merge queries overview - Microsoft Learn | Merge queries overview - Microsoft Learn

q134.stem: You have a Power BI semantic model with four queries: Query1, Query2, Query3 and Query4. Query1 loads customer data into the model and is referenced by the other three queries. You discover that data refresh for the model is slow. You need to improve the refresh time while minimizing costs. What should you do?
options: Run the Table.buffer function in Query1.
Duplicate Query1 to all the other queries.
Reconfigure Query1 as a dataflow entity.
From the Power BI Admin portal, increase the Capacity settings.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Reconfigure Query1 as a dataflow entity.

Why it is correct: since Query1 is referenced by three others it is evaluated several times per refresh; moving it to a dataflow processes it once and the other queries read its stored result, with no extra capacity cost.

⚠️ Heads-up: the community is split (C 68%, A 32%); the source key is C. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Introduction to dataflows - Microsoft Learn | Table.Buffer (M) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Run the Table.buffer function in Query1. — Why it is incorrect: Table.Buffer caches the table in memory during one query’s evaluation but is not shared across separate queries and usually does not solve this case.
  • Option B — Duplicate Query1 to all the other queries. — Why it is incorrect: duplicating Query1 multiplies load and maintenance.
  • Option D — From the Power BI Admin portal, increase the Capacity settings. — Why it is incorrect: increasing capacity adds cost, and the requirement is to minimize it.

q135.stem:
You have an organization dimension named DimOrganizations and four related tables (DimOrgVertical, DimOrgSubVertical, DimOrganizations and FactSales) as shown, chained by one-to-many relationships. Select the options that complete each statement. NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

1) The tables represent a [choice] dimension.
2) [choice] is the only table that supports a hierarchy model for DimOrgVertical.

answer.correct:

  • The tables represent a … dimension: snowflake
  • Table that supports the hierarchy for DimOrgVertical: DimOrgSubVertical
  • Snowflake: a dimension normalized across chained related tables (Vertical → SubVertical → Organizations) is a snowflake.

q136.stem:
You have a Power BI semantic model with an Opportunity table. The Qualification column contains values between 0 and 1. You need a measure that scores opportunities on a scale of low, medium and high. How should you complete the DAX formula? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

Sales Qualification =
IF(
  'Opportunity'[Qualification] < 0.5,
  "Low",
  [A] (
    'Opportunity'[Qualification] > 0.7,
    [B],
    [C]
  )
)

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • [A]: IF.EAGER
  • [B]: HIGH
  • [C]: MEDIUM
  • IF.EAGER: nested condition that evaluates both branches up front (valid with the same three arguments).
  • HIGH if above 0.7 and MEDIUM otherwise (between 0.5 and 0.7).

⚠️ Heads-up: a normal nested IF would also work; the source key marks IF.EAGER. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: IF.EAGER (DAX) - Microsoft Learn | IF (DAX) - Microsoft Learn

q137.stem: You have a Power BI semantic model that connects to a streaming data source updated frequently. You need a report that supports real-time analytics, minimizes the performance impact on the data source and displays the most recent data without performing a data refresh. Which connectivity mode should you use for the dataset?
options: DirectQuery mode
Import mode
LiveConnect mode
Push mode

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Push mode

Why it is correct: a push (streaming) dataset receives data directly into Power BI, so visuals show the latest data without refreshing or querying the source on each interaction.

⚠️ Heads-up: the community is split (D 47%, A 43%); the source key is D. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Real-time streaming in Power BI - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — DirectQuery mode — Why it is incorrect: DirectQuery queries the source on each interaction, increasing load on it. Official documentation: DirectQuery in Power BI - Microsoft Learn
  • Option B — Import mode — Why it is incorrect: Import requires scheduled refreshes, so it does not show the latest without refreshing.
  • Option C — LiveConnect mode — Why it is incorrect: LiveConnect is used with Analysis Services, not streaming sources.

q138.stem:
You have a Power BI semantic model with an Item table containing a Quantity column. You need a DAX query that meets: item rank is calculated by Quantity; ranking must NOT skip positions when two or more items have the same Quantity; if an item is unfiltered, the total Quantity must display a blank value. How should you complete the formula? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

Item Quantity Rank =
IF( [A] ( 'Item'[Item] ),
  RANKX( ALL('Item'[Item]), [Quantity], , , [B] )
)

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • [A]: SELECTEDVALUE
  • [B]: DENSE
  • SELECTEDVALUE: source key; returns the value when a single item is in context and blank otherwise.
  • DENSE: dense ranking, no gaps after ties (SKIP leaves gaps).

⚠️ Heads-up: the usual pattern to test for a single item is HASONEVALUE; the source image marks SELECTEDVALUE. Please review. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: SELECTEDVALUE (DAX) - Microsoft Learn | RANKX (DAX) - Microsoft Learn

q139.stem:
You use Power Query Editor to pull data from a SharePoint Online list and plan to use the Advanced Editor to build an M query. You need a query that loads the data, expands a column named Location and hides a column named CountryOrRegion from the dataset. How should you complete the query? NOTE: each correct answer is worth one point.

#"Expanded Location" = [A]( #"3b73bb0e-…", "Location", {"DisplayName"}, {"Location.DisplayName"} ),
#"Removed" = [B]( #"Expanded Location", { "CountryOrRegion" } )

answer.correct:

  • [A]: Table.ExpandRecordColumn
  • [B]: Table.RemoveColumns
  • Table.ExpandRecordColumn: Location is a record column; this function takes the fields to extract and the new names, as in the code.
  • Table.RemoveColumns: removes the named column from the dataset.

⚠️ Heads-up: in the source solution image the first option (Table.ExpandListColumn) appears to be marked, but the syntax with fields and new names only fits ExpandRecordColumn; the latter is marked. Please review. Check it against the linked documentation.

q140.stem:
You have a Power BI semantic model with two tables, Category (Category, Color, Listing, StoreNumber) and Purchases (PurchaseDate, PurchaseQuantity, Refresh, StoreNumber), with a many-to-one and a many-to-many relationship as shown. Select the options that complete each statement. NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

1) Cross filter direction for the many-to-one relationship is set to [choice].

Visual display

q225.stem: In Power BI Desktop you are creating a report with three pages and need to create a custom tooltip page and prepare it for use. Which three actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

q226.stem: You need to use AI insights to add a column of enhanced data based on customer feedback. q227.stem: You have a Power BI report named ReportA and a tenant that allows users to export data. You need to ensure that consumers of ReportA cannot export any data from visuals. Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

q228.stem: You have a Power BI report that will be rendered on a vertical display. You need to maximize the portion of the screen area used by the report. What should you do?

q229.stem: You need to create a visual that compares profit across 10 product categories for a selected quarter. What is the best visual to use to achieve the goal?

q230.stem: You have a Power BI dataset named Finance hosted in a Power BI workspace. The finance team is NOT a member of any workspace roles. You need to enable the finance team to use Microsoft Excel to analyze the Finance dataset. What should you do?
options: Grant the finance team build permissions to the Finance dataset.

Create a row-level security (RLS) role and add the finance team to the role as members.
Grant the finance team write permissions to the Finance dataset.

  • Option D — Grant the finance team write permissions to the Finance dataset. — Why it is incorrect: write permission lets users modify the dataset, not just query it.

q231.stem: You have a Power BI report with a visual that contains a measure. You need to ensure that all values are set to two decimal places and all negative values are displayed in red font and parentheses. Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: For the visual, apply conditional formatting to the background color.
Configure the measure to use a custom format.

q233.stem: You have a Power BI report with a page containing a card, a matrix and a bar chart. q234.stem: You have a Power BI model with tables Population (PopulationAmount, DateKey; DateKey contains the first day of each year and is used for a many-to-one relationship with Date) and Date, and the measures Total Population = SUM('Population'[PopulationAmount]) and 2023 Population = CALCULATE([Total Population], 'Date'[Year] = 2023). You create a table visual displaying Date[Year] and [2023 Population]. What will the table visual show?
options: one row per year that contains blank values for every year except 2023
one row per date that contains the population value for the corresponding year repeated in each row
a single row for the year 2023 that contains the related population value
one row per year that contains the same value repeated for each year

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: one row per year that contains the same value repeated for each year

Why it is correct: the Date[Year] = 2023 filter in CALCULATE replaces the Year filter context supplied by each row, so every row returns the 2023 population.

  • Option B — one row per date that contains the population value for the corresponding year repeated in each row — Why it is incorrect: the visual groups by year, not by date.
  • Option C — a single row for the year 2023 that contains the related population value — Why it is incorrect: the table shows one row per Date year, not just 2023.

q235.stem: You have a Power BI dataset with quarterly sales performance data. You need to enable managers to review the data in a format that is optimized for printing and renders data in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint and PDF formats. What should you create?

q237.stem: You have a Power BI report with a line chart that displays sales data for several regions. You need to add an element that enables users to filter the sales data to include only a selected region. Which two elements achieve the goal? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

q238.stem: You plan to use Power BI to create a quarterly profit report that: emphasizes the percentage of total profits contributed by each product category in dollars and as a percentage; and compares profit margins across sales regions. Which type of visual should you use for each requirement?

q241.stem: You have a Power BI workspace with a semantic model and a report named Sales report. All users in the sales department are assigned the Viewer role for the workspace. q244.stem: You have a Power BI report with the table shown (“Current Month Returns in USD”), with conditional formatting using colored icons (red, yellow, green) showing which stores are above, near or below the monthly returns quota. q245.stem: You have a Power BI report that contains one visual. You need to provide users with the ability to change the visual type without affecting the view for other users. What should you do?

q246.stem: You have a Power BI report with the table visual in the first exhibit (OrderDate, Total Sales, Total Cost). q247.stem: You have a Power BI report that contains a card showing the year-to-date revenue value. You need to ensure screen reader users can read the value when initially interacting with the card. The value must stay updated as the dataset is refreshed. What should you do?

q248.stem: You have a Power BI report with a table visual containing a column of whole numbers from 1 to 20. q249.stem: You use Power Query Editor to preview the data in a column named Resource Location. q250.stem: You have a Power BI report with the visual shown (Product/Sales table with red and green backgrounds). You need to make the visual more accessible to users who have color vision deficiency. What should you do?

q251.stem: You have a Power BI app that contains a report named Report1. You add a new page to Report1. You need to ensure that users can view the new page. The solution must minimize administrative effort. What should you do?

  • Option C — Inline hierarchy labels — Why it is incorrect: unrelated to links.
  • Option D — URL icons — Why it is incorrect: URL icons show an icon, not the site name.

q253.stem: You use Power Query Editor to review a query that contains a column named Country. You need to view, in the Data preview, the percentage of values that contain errors and the count of empty values. What should you enable? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Percentage of values with errors: Calidad de columna
  • Count of empty values: Perfil de columna
  • Error percentage → Column quality: shows % valid, error and empty.
  • Empty count → Column profile: its statistics include Count, Error, Empty, Distinct, Unique…

⚠️ Heads-up: the source solution image marks “Column distribution” and “Column quality”, which does not match the docs (distribution does not show error %; the empty count appears in the profile). Quality + Profile is marked; please review. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Data profiling tools - Microsoft Learn

q254.stem: You have a Power BI semantic model Model1 containing the fields Sales and Quarter and a DAX measure that sums Sales. You need to create a report with the “Sales By Quarter” visual shown (100% stacked areas by Category). The solution must NOT require additional DAX measures. Which type of visual should you use?
options: Ribbon chart
Line chart
100% stacked area chart
Area chart

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 100% stacked area chart

Why it is correct: the 100% stacked area chart shows each category's share along the axis with no extra measures.

  • Official documentation: Visualization types in Power BI - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Ribbon chart — Why it is incorrect: shows rank with ribbons, not 100% areas.
  • Option B — Line chart — Why it is incorrect: shows absolute values, not proportions.
  • Option D — Area chart — Why it is incorrect: shows absolute values, not 100%.

q255.stem: You have a Power BI semantic model that contains a table. You need to create a report page with two visuals: Visual 1 displays the distribution of hierarchical data; Visual 2 lets users search and then filter by values. Which type should you choose for each visual? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Visual 1: ('Gráfico de rectángulos (Treemap)', 'Treemap')
  • Visual 2: ('Segmentación (Slicer)', 'Slicer')
  • Visual 1 → Treemap: shows hierarchical data as nested rectangles.
  • Visual 2 → Slicer: lets users search and filter by values.
  • Official documentation: Treemaps - Microsoft Learn | Slicers - Microsoft Learn

q256.stem: You use Power Query Editor to review the query shown. Each Region value appears only on the row where it first occurred; each subsequent occurrence is blank. You need to ensure every row contains the correct non-blank value, minimizing development effort. Which column should you select and which action should you perform? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Column: Region
  • Action: ('Rellenar hacia abajo', 'Fill down')
  • Column → Region (the one with blanks).
  • Action → Fill down: copies the last non-blank value to the rows below.
  • Official documentation: Fill values in a column - Microsoft Learn

q257.stem: You have a Power BI report that contains a bar chart displaying sales by country. You need to ensure that a summary of the data shown on the bar chart is accessible by using a screen reader. What should you configure on the bar chart?
options: Conditional formatting
Alt text
The tab order
The layer order

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Alt text

Why it is correct: alt text describes the visual to screen readers, including a summary of the data.

⚠️ Heads-up: the OCR key is “C” (tab order), but a screen-reader summary is configured with alt text (B; community vote B). Please review. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Create accessible reports - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Conditional formatting — Why it is incorrect: conditional formatting is visual and not read by screen readers.
  • Option C — The tab order — Why it is incorrect: tab order sets navigation order, not a summary.
  • Option D — The layer order — Why it is incorrect: layer order affects visual stacking.

q258.stem: You have a Power BI tenant that hosts the datasets in the table: Sales (sales targets, sales data, employee salary data; daily performance reports and quarterly reports to calculate bonuses), Operations (environmental sensor data; reports showing average sensor readings over time) and Finance (financial transaction data; budget planning and monthly board reports). Requirements: export of reports containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) must be prevented; data used for financial decisions must be reviewed and approved before use. For each statement, select Yes if true. NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • The Sales dataset requires a sensitivity label.: Yes
  • The Operations dataset requires a sensitivity label and must be certified.: No
  • The Finance dataset requires a sensitivity label and must be certified.: Yes
  • Sales → Yes: contains salaries (PII); a sensitivity label can restrict export.
  • Operations → No: sensor data, no PII and no financial decisions.
  • Finance → Yes: financial decisions require review/approval (certification) and financial data warrants a label.
  • Official documentation: Sensitivity labels - Microsoft Learn | Certify content - Microsoft Learn

q259.stem: You have a Power BI tenant. You have reports that use financial datasets and are exported as PDF files. You need to ensure that the reports are encrypted. What should you implement?
options: Microsoft Intune policies
Row-level security (RLS)
Sensitivity labels
Dataset certifications

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Sensitivity labels

Why it is correct: sensitivity labels can apply encryption and are carried to exports such as PDF.

⚠️ Heads-up: the OCR key is doubtful; the community votes C (sensitivity labels). Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Sensitivity labels - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Microsoft Intune policies — Why it is incorrect: Intune manages devices/apps; it does not encrypt exported files.
  • Option B — Row-level security (RLS) — Why it is incorrect: RLS restricts visible rows; it does not encrypt files.
  • Option D — Dataset certifications — Why it is incorrect: certification signals trust; it does not encrypt.

q260.stem: You have a Microsoft Excel file on a file server. You create a Power BI report and import a table from the Excel file. You publish the report. You need to ensure that the data refreshes every four hours. What should you do first?
options: Upload the Excel file to a Power BI workspace.
Create a subscription to the report.
Deploy an on-premises data gateway.
Edit the data source credentials.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Deploy an on-premises data gateway.

Why it is correct: a file on an on-premises server requires a gateway to schedule service refresh.

  • Official documentation: What is an on-premises data gateway? - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Upload the Excel file to a Power BI workspace. — Why it is incorrect: uploading would break the link to the server and not automate refresh.
  • Option B — Create a subscription to the report. — Why it is incorrect: subscriptions send emails; they do not refresh data.
  • Option D — Edit the data source credentials. — Why it is incorrect: credentials are needed afterwards, but without a gateway the source is unreachable.

links.t: What is an on-premises data gateway?

q261.stem: You have a dataset that is used infrequently and refreshes every hour. You receive a notification that the refresh was disabled due to inactivity. Which two actions will cause the scheduled refresh to resume? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
options: Enable query caching for the dataset.
Import the dataset to Microsoft Excel.
From the Power BI service, open a dashboard that uses the dataset.
From the Power BI service, open a report that uses the dataset.
From PowerShell, run the Get-PowerBIReport cmdlet.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option C: From the Power BI service, open a dashboard that uses the dataset.
  • Option D: From the Power BI service, open a report that uses the dataset.

Why it is correct: the refresh resumes when a user visits a dashboard or report that uses the dataset.

  • Official documentation: Configure scheduled refresh - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Enable query caching for the dataset. — Why it is incorrect: query caching does not re-enable the schedule.
  • Option B — Import the dataset to Microsoft Excel. — Why it is incorrect: exporting to Excel does not re-enable refresh.
  • Option E — From PowerShell, run the Get-PowerBIReport cmdlet. — Why it is incorrect: the cmdlet only lists reports; it does not count as a visit.

q262.stem: You have a Power BI workspace with a dataset, a report and a dashboard. External users can access the dashboard; managers the dashboard and a manager report; employees the dashboard and an RLS-constrained report. You need all users, including external users, to be able to tag workspace administrators if they identify an issue with the dashboard, and other users must see the issues raised. What should you use?
options: Comments
Chat in Microsoft Teams
Alerts
Subscriptions

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Comments

Why it is correct: comments let you @mention people and remain visible to other users with access.

⚠️ Heads-up: option A is cut off in the OCR; it is read as “Comments” (key A, 100% community). Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Add comments to dashboards and reports - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Chat in Microsoft Teams — Why it is incorrect: Teams chat is not visible on the dashboard and externals may not have Teams.
  • Option C — Alerts — Why it is incorrect: alerts notify on data thresholds, not issues.
  • Option D — Subscriptions — Why it is incorrect: subscriptions send emailed copies.

links.t: Add comments to dashboards and reports

q263.stem: You have a PBIX file that imports several tables from an Azure SQL database. The data will be migrated to another Azure SQL database. You need to change the connections in the PBIX file. The solution must minimize administrative effort. What should you do?
options: From Power Query Editor, create new queries.
From Power Query Editor, modify the source of each query.
Create a PBIT file, open the file, and change the data sources when prompted.
Modify the Data source settings.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Modify the Data source settings.

Why it is correct: “Data source settings” lets you change the source once and applies to all queries that use it.

  • Official documentation: Data sources in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — From Power Query Editor, create new queries. — Why it is incorrect: recreating queries is unnecessary effort.
  • Option B — From Power Query Editor, modify the source of each query. — Why it is incorrect: each query has to be edited one by one.
  • Option C — Create a PBIT file, open the file, and change the data sources when prompted. — Why it is incorrect: more steps than changing the source directly (and the template needs parameters).

links.t: Data sources in Power BI Desktop

q264.stem: You have a Power BI workspace that contains several reports. You need to provide a user with the ability to create a dashboard that will use the visuals from the reports. What should you do?
options: Create a row-level security (RLS) role and add the user to the role.
Share the reports with the user.
Grant the Read permission for the datasets to the user.
Add the user as a member of the workspace.
Add the user as a Viewer of the workspace.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Add the user as a member of the workspace.

Why it is correct: creating dashboards in a workspace requires a role that can edit content (Contributor, Member or Admin); Member qualifies.

  • Official documentation: Roles in workspaces - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Create a row-level security (RLS) role and add the user to the role. — Why it is incorrect: RLS filters rows; it does not grant authoring rights.
  • Option B — Share the reports with the user. — Why it is incorrect: sharing gives read access; it does not allow building dashboards from its visuals.
  • Option C — Grant the Read permission for the datasets to the user. — Why it is incorrect: dataset Read permission does not allow pinning report visuals.
  • Option E — Add the user as a Viewer of the workspace. — Why it is incorrect: Viewers can only view content.

q265.stem: You have a Power BI workspace that contains a single-page report named Sales. You need to add all the visuals from Sales to a dashboard. The solution must ensure that additional visuals added to the page are added automatically to the dashboard. Which three actions should you perform in sequence?

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Step 1: ('Abrir powerbi.com', 'Open powerbi.com')
  • Step 2: ('Abrir el informe Sales', 'Open the Sales report')
  • Step 3: ('Anclar la página', 'Pin the page')
  1. Open powerbi.com (the service).
  2. Open the Sales report.
  3. Pin the page (live tile): changes to the page sync to the dashboard.
  • Official documentation: Pin a whole report page (live tile) - Microsoft Learn

links.t: Pin a whole report page (live tile)

q266.stem: You have a report in Power BI named report1 that is based on a shared dataset. You need to minimize the risk of data exfiltration for report1. The solution must prevent other reports from being affected. What should you do?
options: Clear Allow recipients to share your dashboard and Allow users to build new content using the underlying datasets for the dataset.
Apply row-level security (RLS) to the shared dataset.
Select the Allow end users to export both summarized and underlying data option for the report.
Select the Don't allow end users to export any data option for the report.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Select the Don't allow end users to export any data option for the report.

Why it is correct: the export setting is per report, so it blocks export only for report1.

  • Official documentation: Report export data options - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Clear Allow recipients to share your dashboard and Allow users to build new content using the underlying datasets for the dataset. — Why it is incorrect: acts on the dataset and would affect other reports.
  • Option B — Apply row-level security (RLS) to the shared dataset. — Why it is incorrect: RLS limits rows; it does not prevent exporting what is visible.
  • Option C — Select the Allow end users to export both summarized and underlying data option for the report. — Why it is incorrect: it increases exfiltration risk.

q267.stem: In Power BI Desktop, you are creating visualizations in a report based on an imported dataset. You need to allow Power BI users to export the summarized data used to create the visualizations but prevent the users from exporting the underlying data. What should you do?
options: From the Power BI service, configure the dataset permissions.
From Power BI Desktop, configure the Data Load settings for the current file.
From Power BI Desktop, modify the data source permissions.
From Power BI Desktop, configure the Report settings for the current file.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: From Power BI Desktop, configure the Report settings for the current file.

Why it is correct: under Options → Report settings (current file) you choose “Allow end users to export summarized data only”.

  • Official documentation: Export data from visuals - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — From the Power BI service, configure the dataset permissions. — Why it is incorrect: dataset permissions do not control the export type.
  • Option B — From Power BI Desktop, configure the Data Load settings for the current file. — Why it is incorrect: Data Load affects import/performance, not export.
  • Option C — From Power BI Desktop, modify the data source permissions. — Why it is incorrect: data source permissions govern source access, not export.

q268.stem: You have a Power BI report that uses row-level security (RLS). You need to transfer RLS membership maintenance to an Azure network security team. The solution must NOT provide the Azure network security team with the ability to manage reports, datasets, or dashboards. What should you do?
options: Grant the Read and Build permissions for the Power BI datasets to the Azure network security team.
Configure custom instructions for the Request access feature that instructs users to contact the Azure network security team.
Instruct the Azure network security team to create security groups. Configure RLS to use the groups.
Add the Azure network security team as members of the RLS role.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Instruct the Azure network security team to create security groups. Configure RLS to use the groups.

Why it is correct: with Azure AD security groups assigned to the RLS role, the team maintains membership in Azure AD with no Power BI permissions.

⚠️ Heads-up: the OCR text of options C and D is partial; check the original wording. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Row-level security (RLS) with Power BI - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Grant the Read and Build permissions for the Power BI datasets to the Azure network security team. — Why it is incorrect: Read/Build does not manage RLS and grants unnecessary data access.
  • Option B — Configure custom instructions for the Request access feature that instructs users to contact the Azure network security team. — Why it is incorrect: it only changes the access-request message.
  • Option D — Add the Azure network security team as members of the RLS role. — Why it is incorrect: being role members makes them RLS subjects, not membership maintainers.

q269.stem: You have four sales regions. Each region has multiple sales managers. You implement RLS in a data model and assign the relevant mail-enabled security group to each role. Managers see their region's records but not others. A sales manager changes to a different region and you must ensure the manager sees the correct sales data. What should you do?
options: Change the Microsoft Power BI license type of the sales manager.
From Power BI Desktop, edit the Row-Level Security setting for the reports.
Manage the permissions of the underlying dataset.
Request that the sales manager be added to the correct Azure Active Directory group.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Request that the sales manager be added to the correct Azure Active Directory group.

Why it is correct: since roles use groups, moving the user to the new region's group is enough.

  • Official documentation: Row-level security (RLS) with Power BI - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Change the Microsoft Power BI license type of the sales manager. — Why it is incorrect: license type does not affect RLS.
  • Option B — From Power BI Desktop, edit the Row-Level Security setting for the reports. — Why it is incorrect: roles are already defined; no need to edit them.
  • Option C — Manage the permissions of the underlying dataset. — Why it is incorrect: dataset permissions do not determine the visible region.

q270.stem: You have more than 100 published datasets. Ten were verified to meet your corporate quality standards. You need to ensure that the 10 verified datasets appear at the top of the list of published datasets whenever users search for existing datasets. What should you do?
options: Promote the datasets.
Certify the datasets.
Feature the dataset on the home page.
Publish the datasets in an app.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Certify the datasets.

Why it is correct: certified datasets are listed first in the data hub and dataset pickers.

  • Official documentation: Endorse your content (promote and certify) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Promote the datasets. — Why it is incorrect: promotion marks content as valuable, but certification ranks higher and implies review.
  • Option C — Feature the dataset on the home page. — Why it is incorrect: featuring is for the home page, not search ordering.
  • Option D — Publish the datasets in an app. — Why it is incorrect: apps do not change the list order.

q271.stem: You have a Power BI workspace. You need to grant the capabilities in the table: User1 — create and publish apps; User2 — publish reports to the workspace and delete dashboards. The solution must use the principle of least privilege. Which role should you assign to each user? NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • User1: ('Miembro', 'Member')
  • User2: ('Colaborador', 'Contributor')
  • User1 → Member: only Admin and Member can publish apps; Member is the least privilege.
  • User2 → Contributor: can create, edit and delete content and publish reports; Viewer can only view.
  • Official documentation: Roles in workspaces - Microsoft Learn

q272.stem: You create a dashboard in the Power BI service with a card showing total sales for the current year. You grant users access via the Viewer role on the workspace. A user wants to receive daily notifications of the number shown on the card. You need to automate the notifications. What should you do?
options: Create a subscription.
Create a data alert.
Share the dashboard with the user.
Tag the user in a comment.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Create a subscription.

Why it is correct: subscriptions email a snapshot of the dashboard on a schedule (e.g. daily).

  • Official documentation: Subscribe to reports and dashboards - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Create a data alert. — Why it is incorrect: alerts fire when a threshold is crossed, not daily.
  • Option C — Share the dashboard with the user. — Why it is incorrect: sharing does not create recurring notifications.
  • Option D — Tag the user in a comment. — Why it is incorrect: a comment is neither automatic nor daily.

q273.stem: You have a Power BI workspace named Workspace1 that contains a dataset named DS1 and a report named RPT1. A user wants to create a report by using the data in DS1 and publish the report to another workspace. You need to provide the user with the appropriate access, minimizing the number of access permissions granted. What should you do?
options: Add the user as a Viewer of Workspace1.
Grant the Build permission for DS1 to the user.
Share RPT1 with the user.
Add the user as a member of Workspace1.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Grant the Build permission for DS1 to the user.

Why it is correct: Build permission lets the user create new content on DS1 from another workspace or Desktop without access to the source workspace.

  • Official documentation: Build permission for datasets - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Add the user as a Viewer of Workspace1. — Why it is incorrect: a Viewer cannot build content on the dataset.
  • Option C — Share RPT1 with the user. — Why it is incorrect: sharing the report does not grant Build on DS1.
  • Option D — Add the user as a member of Workspace1. — Why it is incorrect: Member grants far more permissions than needed.

q274.stem:
Note: this question is part of a series with the same scenario; each question has a unique solution that might or might not meet the goals.

You have five reports and two dashboards in a workspace. You need to grant all organizational users read access to one dashboard and three reports.

Solution: You publish an app to the entire organization. Does this meet the goal?
options: Yes
No

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Yes

Why it is correct: publishing an app lets you choose the included items (one dashboard and three reports) and the audience (entire organization) with read-only access.

⚠️ Heads-up: community votes split (A 6, B 4); Yes is kept as the standard way to distribute selected content. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Create and publish apps - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — No — Why it is incorrect: it does meet the goal: the app lets you select content and audience.

q275.stem:
Note: this question is part of a series with the same scenario; each question has a unique solution that might or might not meet the goals.

You have five reports and two dashboards in a workspace. You need to grant all organizational users read access to one dashboard and three reports.

Solution: You enable “Included in app” for all assets. Does this meet the goal?
options: Yes
No

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: No

Why it is correct: marking “Included in app” would include all items (5 reports and 2 dashboards) and by itself does not publish the app or set the audience.

  • Official documentation: Create and publish apps - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Yes — Why it is incorrect: it would include all content, not just one dashboard and three reports.

q276.stem:
Note: this question is part of a series with the same scenario; each question has a unique solution that might or might not meet the goals.

You have five reports and two dashboards in a workspace. You need to grant all organizational users read access to one dashboard and three reports.

Solution: You assign all the users the Viewer role to the workspace. Does this meet the goal?
options: Yes
No

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: No

Why it is correct: the Viewer role gives access to all workspace content (5 reports and 2 dashboards), not just one dashboard and three reports.

  • Official documentation: Roles in workspaces - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Yes — Why it is incorrect: it grants more access than required.

q277.stem: From Power BI Desktop, you publish a new dataset and report to a Power BI workspace. The dataset has an RLS role named HR. You need to ensure that HR team members have RLS applied when they view reports based on the dataset. What should you do?
options: From powerbi.com, add users to the HR role for the dataset.
From powerbi.com, share the dataset to the HR team members.
From Power BI Desktop, change the Row-Level Security settings.
From Power BI Desktop, import a table that contains the HR team members.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: From powerbi.com, add users to the HR role for the dataset.

Why it is correct: RLS role membership is assigned in the service (dataset Security).

  • Official documentation: Row-level security (RLS) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — From powerbi.com, share the dataset to the HR team members. — Why it is incorrect: sharing does not assign users to the role.
  • Option C — From Power BI Desktop, change the Row-Level Security settings. — Why it is incorrect: Desktop defines roles, not members.
  • Option D — From Power BI Desktop, import a table that contains the HR team members. — Why it is incorrect: importing a table does not assign role membership.

q278.stem: You have a Power BI dashboard that monitors the quality of manufacturing processes, with a line chart of defective products by day and a KPI visual showing the current daily percentage of defective products. You need to be notified when the daily percentage exceeds 3%. What should you create?
options: A subscription
An alert
A smart narrative visual
A Q&A visual

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: An alert

Why it is correct: data alerts (on KPI, card, gauge tiles) notify when a threshold is crossed.

  • Official documentation: Data alerts in the Power BI service - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — A subscription — Why it is incorrect: subscriptions send scheduled snapshots without evaluating a threshold.
  • Option C — A smart narrative visual — Why it is incorrect: smart narrative only summarizes; it does not notify.
  • Option D — A Q&A visual — Why it is incorrect: Q&A does not send notifications.

links.t: Data alerts in the Power BI service

q279.stem: You create a report in Power BI Desktop using data from an SSAS cube on your company's internal network. You plan to publish it to the Power BI service. What should you implement to ensure users of the service have the most up-to-date data from the cube?
options: An OData feed
An on-premises data gateway
A subscription
A scheduled refresh of the dataset

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: An on-premises data gateway

Why it is correct: SSAS is queried live/refreshed through an on-premises gateway; without it the service cannot reach the internal network.

⚠️ Heads-up: scheduled refresh (D) would also be needed for an import model; with a live connection the gateway suffices. Key B (100% community) is followed. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: On-premises data gateway - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — An OData feed — Why it is incorrect: not applicable to an SSAS cube.
  • Option C — A subscription — Why it is incorrect: subscriptions do not refresh data.
  • Option D — A scheduled refresh of the dataset — Why it is incorrect: scheduled refresh also needs a gateway for on-premises sources.

q280.stem: You have five sales regions, each with a single salesperson. An imported dataset has a dynamic RLS role named Sales filtering by salesperson. You publish the dataset, set role membership and distribute. A salesperson believes she should see more data. You need to verify what data she currently sees. What should you do?
options: Use the Test as role option to view data as the salesperson's user account.
Use the Test as role option to view data as the Sales role.
Instruct the salesperson to open the report in Power BI Desktop.
Filter the data in the reports to match the intended logic in the filter on the sales transaction table.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Use the Test as role option to view data as the salesperson's user account.

Why it is correct: with dynamic RLS the role alone does not represent a person; test as her user account.

  • Official documentation: Validate RLS roles (Test as role) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Use the Test as role option to view data as the Sales role. — Why it is incorrect: the role without a user does not evaluate the salesperson's USERPRINCIPALNAME().
  • Option C — Instruct the salesperson to open the report in Power BI Desktop. — Why it is incorrect: Desktop does not apply her RLS.
  • Option D — Filter the data in the reports to match the intended logic in the filter on the sales transaction table. — Why it is incorrect: manual filtering does not verify the actual RLS.

q281.stem: You have multiple dashboards. You need to ensure that when users browse the available dashboards from powerbi.com, they can see which dashboards contain PII, minimizing configuration effort and impact on the dashboard design. What should you use?
options: Microsoft Information Protection sensitivity labels
Tiles
Comments
Active Directory groups

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Microsoft Information Protection sensitivity labels

Why it is correct: sensitivity labels show next to the dashboard in lists without changing its design.

  • Official documentation: Sensitivity labels - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Tiles — Why it is incorrect: tiles change the design and are not visible in the list.
  • Option C — Comments — Why it is incorrect: comments are not visible when browsing the list.
  • Option D — Active Directory groups — Why it is incorrect: groups control access; they do not flag content.

q282.stem: You have a dataset with the permissions shown in the exhibit (Ben Smith: Owner; corp group: Read, Reshare, Build; finance group: Read, Build). Select the answer choice that completes each statement. NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

q285.stem: You publish a dataset to the Power BI service with a connection to an on-premises SQL Server database. q287.stem: You have two workspaces, WorkspaceA (datasets Sales and HR) and WorkspaceB. q288.stem: You have a Power BI workspace named BI Data that contains a dataset named BI Finance. You have the Build permission for BI Finance but NO permissions for the workspace. q289.stem: You use Power Query Editor to load two queries. Query1 results in: “Expression.Error: The column 'Sales' of the table wasn't found”. q290.stem: You create a report in Power BI Desktop using data from an SSAS tabular model on your company's internal network. You plan to publish it to the Power BI service. What should you implement to ensure users have the most up-to-date data from the tabular model?

q291.stem: You have a semantic model with the permissions shown (Ben Smith: Owner; corp: Read, Reshare, Build; finance: Read, Build). Select the answer choice that completes each statement. NOTE: each correct selection is worth one point.

q292.stem: You have a Power BI semantic model named Model1 that contains sales data. You need to ensure that Model1 is refreshed on the first day of each month to include last month's sales data. What should you configure?

q293.stem: You have a Power BI workspace named Workspace1 and a group named Group1. You need to ensure that the members of Group1 are notified when there are issues in Workspace1. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege. What should you do?

q295.stem: You are creating a new semantic model in Power BI Desktop. You connect to a recently used data source and receive an error that the password is expired. You need to update the credentials. What should you do?

q297.stem: You have a Power BI tenant with workspace WS1 containing semantic model SM1; reports RPT1, RPT2 and RPT3 (connected to SM1); and dashboard DB1 with content from RPT1 and RPT2. q299.stem: You have a Power BI semantic model. You need to configure RLS to restrict data access for users that have Viewer permissions. Which three actions should you perform in sequence?

q301.stem: Litware case study. You need to create the required relationship for the executives' visual. What should you do before you can create the relationship?

q302.stem: Litware case study. You need to get data from the Microsoft SQL Server tables. What should you use to configure the connection?

DirectQuery that uses the end-user's credentials

q303.stem: Contoso case study. You need to create the relationship between the product list and the revenue results. The solution must minimize the time it takes to render visuals. What should you set as the relationship cardinality?

q305.stem: Contoso case study. Once the profit and loss dataset is created, which four actions should you perform in sequence to ensure that the business unit analysts see the appropriate profit and loss data?

q306.stem: Contoso case study. Which DAX expression should you use to get the ending balances in the balance sheet reports?
options: CALCULATE( SUM( BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount] ), LASTDATE( 'Date'[Date] ) )
CALCULATE( SUM( BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount] ), DATESQTD( 'Date'[Date] ) )
FIRSTNONBLANK( 'Date'[Date], SUM( BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount] ) )
CALCULATE( MAX( BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount] ), LASTDATE( 'Date'[Date] ) )

answer.incorrect:

q307.stem: Litware case study. You need to create relationships to meet the reporting requirements of the customer service department (filter by sales month and ship month independently). What should you create?

A one-to-many relationship from Sales[sales_date_id] to Date[date_id] and a one-to-many relationship from Sales[sales_ship_date_id] to Date[date_id].

An additional date table named ShipDate, a one-to-many relationship from Date[date_id] to Sales[sales_date_id], and a one-to-many relationship from ShipDate[date_id] to Sales[sales_ship_date_id].

q308.stem: Litware case study. You need to provide a solution to provide the sales managers with the required access. What should you include in the solution?
options: Create a security role that has a table filter on the Sales_Manager table where username = UserName().
